name: Instapage
tagline: Landing pages, personalization, experiments, collaboration, and analytics

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Create
tiers.limits: 15,000 unique visitors/month; unlimited pages/conversions/contacts; 10 team members; 2 subdomains; 1 workspace; 15,000 email sends/month

tiers.name: Optimize
tiers.limits: 30,000 unique visitors/month at base usage; unlimited pages/conversions/contacts; 10 team members; 2 subdomains; 1 workspace; 30,000 email sends/month
tiers.notes: A 50,000-visitor expanded option and custom higher usage are available; the live page did not expose the expanded dollar price in accessible text.

tiers.name: Convert
tiers.limits: Custom visitors, team/workspace limits and enterprise features; root-domain publishing, heatmaps, global elements, SLA and services

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day Create/Optimize trial capped at 2,500 unique visitors and requiring a credit card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (up to 20% off); custom usage above the expanded Optimize tier is annual-contract-only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Optimize pricing rises with visitor volume (30,000 base, 50,000 expanded, then custom); hitting the 2,500-visitor trial cap ends the trial and transitions to the selected paid plan.

verdictSummary: The visible enterprise landing pages loop is buildable, but a credible replacement needs more than the first screen. Instapage earns its keep through editor, CMS, hosting, polish, so expect a weekend or multi-day build and a narrower personal scope.
coreLoopDIY: Build a focused enterprise landing pages generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
replacementScope: narrow personal or very small-team substitute
whyPeopleStillPay: Instapage: A single site is easy to code. People pay for safe ongoing edits, templates, publishing, domains, collaboration, and no-maintenance hosting.
ongoingBurden: Maintain responsive rendering, browser compatibility, deployment, domains, forms, spam protection, backups, and editor migrations.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Landing pages, forms, dynamic content, analytics and real split tests for free; in return, you operate a marketing database.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Three funnels, a custom domain, forms and one split test for zero dollars; personalization is basic.

rejectedAlternatives.name: GrapesJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It can power an editor after engineering; it does not ship experiments, analytics or collaboration.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Webstudio
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Builds pages, but not the experiments, personalization and campaign analytics this app is bought for.

notes: Useful boundary case: the first 60 percent of Instapage is approachable, but operating the last 40 percent is the real subscription.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow personal substitute for Instapage, not a full clone.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + SQLite.
Primary job: Build a focused enterprise landing pages generator that edits structured page sections, previews responsive layouts, and publishes static files.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: general-purpose visual editing; large template and component libraries; CMS collaboration and client handoff.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
